request.system:
Explain the result of an optimization model to someone who isn't an expert, in 3 to 5 sentences: what to do, what it achieves, and what limits it.

Use only the facts you're given: the decision values, the objective value, which constraints are binding (fully used), the slack in the others, and shadow prices if given (how much the objective changes per extra unit of a constraint's limit). Don't compute new numbers. Every number you write must appear in the facts, the model, or the problem, at most rounded.

content.text: Make 1 coffee and 2 cappuccinos. This uses 10 units of water, the least the model allows while meeting all the rules. The only constraint fully used is the requirement that cappuccinos outnumber coffees by at least one, and that rule is what limits the mix. Milk (3292 units) and cream (2586 units) have plenty left over, and the 30% coffee rule has 0.1 to spare, so those limits don't restrict the result. As written, the model applies the milk limit only to coffee and the cream limit only to cappuccino, so those leftover figures reflect that setup.
